rationale: The candidate is coherent enough as a compact low-rise mass, but the four-view set reads as a fairly generic split box with only a modest carved center rather than a strongly programmed neighborhood building. The mass is more coherent in plan than in section: the top view shows a split-wing/courtyard idea, yet the elevations do not clearly express an active ground threshold on the verified access edge, and the void remains visually shallow relative to the solid. It does respond to the parcel better than a pure bounding-box fill, but the dominant gesture is still somewhat box-like and the access/public edge is semantically weak. Programmatically, neighborhood living can work with this kind of mass, but the visible form does not yet convincingly carry the required active ground edge, public space, and upper hierarchy without further articulation. The references reinforce a useful principle: low-rise interlocking masses around a real court or terrace, with a bridge or lifted connection, are more program-aligned than a sealed split block. The candidate therefore fails hard program fit as shown, though it is close enough to repair toward a suitable neighborhood court/terrace typology.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a central void and an upper bridge-like connection can support a neighborhood program while keeping a legible public threshold.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/campus-like arrangement around a shared open core suggests a more public ground and distributed massing without becoming a tower.

warnings: The thick blue frontage edge is not answered by a clearly legible public void or entry seam in the visible massing.

If repaired, preserve the dominant split-wing/courtyard gesture and make the access edge materially open.
